description: Market-structure scores are directional 1-5 reads for market-map strategy: attractiveness and growth are better when higher; competition, resource intensity, and distribution difficulty are harder when higher.

markets.name: Prediction-Market Prime Brokerage
markets.summary: Cross-venue APIs are emerging; unified collateral, margin, custody, and settlement remain underbuilt — but the non-custodial TERMINAL wedge is now contested: River Markets (YC-backed, institutional clients, live on 3 venues) took exactly the funded-account-orchestration entry this row prescribed.
markets.profit_wedge: Start with funded-account orchestration, risk limits, and position/margin views before attempting true cross-venue clearing.

markets.name: Neutral Event-Market Data Vendor
markets.summary: Prediction markets need clean reference data, contract metadata, histories, resolution criteria, and cross-venue normalization.
markets.profit_wedge: The wedge is not prices alone; it is canonical contract identity, settlement/rules metadata, and historical curves suitable for backtesting.

markets.name: Retail Brokerage & Execution
markets.summary: Huge pools of users and assets, but customer acquisition, regulation, payment-for-order-flow economics, and incumbent brands dominate.
markets.profit_wedge: Niche audiences, embedded brokerage, or a new asset class beat launching another generic equities broker.

markets.name: Market Data Infrastructure
markets.summary: Ticker plants, feed handlers, and low-latency market data are lucrative but dominated by incumbents, exchange licenses, and colocation economics.
markets.profit_wedge: Wedges exist around underserved asset classes, developer ergonomics, and derived analytics, not core exchange feed redistribution.

markets.name: Alternative Data Vendors
markets.summary: Funds will pay for alpha, but signal decay, data rights, compliance review, and procurement friction make repeatable scale hard.
markets.profit_wedge: Own a proprietary source with durable rights, or sell workflow/context instead of a one-off alpha feed.

markets.name: Institutional Crypto Market Infrastructure
markets.summary: Institutions want custody, execution, credit, settlement, and risk across venues, but trust and regulatory posture separate winners.
markets.profit_wedge: Prime brokerage, portfolio margin, collateral mobility, and compliance tooling are stronger wedges than another exchange connector.

markets.name: Indices & Benchmarks
markets.summary: Benchmarks compound through brand, regulation, ETF assets, and licensing, but new entrants need a new asset class or distribution channel.
markets.profit_wedge: Build benchmarks for emerging markets, crypto, private assets, or prediction/event curves where incumbent index brands have not yet standardized the category.

markets.name: Clearing, Custody & Settlement
markets.summary: Post-trade infrastructure can be extremely durable, but licenses, risk capital, regulation, and trust make it hard to enter.
markets.profit_wedge: The best new wedges are in new asset classes or interoperability, not directly competing with OCC/DTCC on mature instruments.
markets.moat: regulatory licenses + network effects + mutualized risk capital

markets.name: Strategy & Asset-Management Platforms
markets.summary: Model marketplaces, strategy wrappers, and managed products can scale, but trust, performance, regulation, and distribution dominate.
markets.profit_wedge: Start with a trusted niche or embedded distribution; generic strategy marketplaces tend to become performance-chasing churn machines.

markets.name: Stablecoin FX & Settlement Rails
markets.summary: The $200T FX settlement stack is unbundling onto stablecoin rails (GENIUS Act legitimized). Winners are licensing + banking + last-mile liquidity NETWORKS, not technology: OpenFX went $4B→$45B in a year on a FalconX-pedigree rolodex. Circle CPN and Stripe/Bridge are platformizing from above.
markets.profit_wedge: None for a non-pedigreed entrant. The play was only ever available to founders arriving with institutional liquidity networks and licensing war chests.
markets.registry_note: screened 2026-07: Zone A finance (balance sheet + licenses); no founder-fit path

markets.name: Reserve Attestation & Proof-of-Reserves
markets.summary: Voluntary post-FTX PoR died in ~6 weeks (Mazars exit); the GENIUS Act's monthly PCAOB-firm reserve examinations turned the same service into a mandated industry. The cleanest demonstration that scandal ignites verification demand but only a mandate converts it into a budget line.
markets.profit_wedge: Attestation tooling + real-time reserve feeds for the accounting firms holding the mandate; grows mechanically with stablecoin float (every OpenFX-style rail adds reserves to attest).

markets.name: Independent Fund-Accounting Verification
markets.summary: Admins checking their own books is a conflicted-party structure (CIBC-Mellon pattern); Arcesium proves giants pay for independence; the sub-$1B tail is unserved. Trust-gated sale, and the seat requires a fund-accounting domain founder — the market is open, the team is the gate.
markets.profit_wedge: AI verification layer reading governing docs (LPA/side letters) against NAV/allocation/fee calcs, sold to fund CFOs as restatement insurance; continuous-NAV trend deepens the need (the checking tools are being built by the admins' own vendors).
markets.moat: clause-to-calc corpus + exam-cited evidence switching costs

markets.name: PIT-Rigorous Public-Records Signals
markets.stage: open wedge in a crowded category
markets.summary: Resolves the tension with the generic Alt Data row (crowded, comp=5): coverage IS crowded, but point-in-time/survivorship integrity is the unclaimed wedge — public records get amended and backdated, so backtests on today's copy embed lookahead. History only accrues forward from when you start snapshotting: a moat competitors cannot buy backward.
markets.profit_wedge: Provably lookahead-free signal feeds from municipal data (permits, deeds, crime) mapped to concentrated tradeable instruments (NYC pure-play REITs, CRE-heavy banks, CMBS). Integrity is the product; the deflation battery is the sales pitch.

markets.name: Tokenized-Securities Transfer & Custody
markets.summary: The securities↔chain boundary is gated by transfer-agent, broker-dealer, and ATS licenses — and traffic is real now (multi-billion tokenized treasuries: BUIDL, Ondo, Franklin). Toll-keeper seats are being taken by licensed platforms; the OpenFX pattern one asset class over.
markets.profit_wedge: Licensed plumbing (TA + custody + ATS) for issuers crossing the boundary; per-crossing and per-AUM fees. Pedigree/licensing-gated like stablecoin FX — entered via acquisition of licenses, not code.
markets.who_pays: issuer (funds pay to cross) + buyer (custody/AUM fees)

markets.name: Alt-Distribution Toll Booths (Accreditation Boundary)
markets.summary: Private-markets access for the wealth channel is gated by accreditation rules, sub-doc plumbing, and fund distribution agreements. iCapital ($200B+ platformed) and CAIS proved the toll-booth economics; tokenization and alts-in-401k policy widen the boundary traffic.
markets.profit_wedge: For entrants: niche boundary segments the duopoly under-serves (evergreen/interval structures, non-US advisors, tokenized feeders) — head-on is closed; distribution relationships are decade-built.
markets.who_pays: issuer (fund sponsors pay for distribution) + buyer (platform fees)

markets.name: Muni Retail Access & Markup Unbundling
markets.summary: Retail muni investors pay ~1%+ dealer markups crossing into a fragmented OTC market gated by dealer inventory networks. Electronic venues (MarketAxess, Tradeweb) unbundled the institutional side; the retail boundary toll persists on ~$4T of outstandings held heavily by households.
markets.profit_wedge: Direct-access or markup-transparency products for RIAs and retail platforms; SEC/MSRB transparency rules are the tripwire that would crack the gate.
markets.who_pays: buyer (embedded markups today; explicit fees post-unbundling)
markets.moat: dealer inventory networks + fragmentation (50k issuers, 1M CUSIPs)

markets.name: Builder-Deployed Markets (HIP-3 class rail-surfing)
markets.summary: A market SHAPE, not a single market: when a platform opens permissionless market deployment (Hyperliquid HIP-3), the first credible deployment of an obvious high-value underlying becomes an acquisition target for the strategic class that will need the capability — before liquidity economics ever have to work. Proven twice in 2026: perpetuals.xyz (HIP-3 FX perps, quietly acquired by OpenFX) and Ornn (compute marketplace/index, anointed by Kalshi settlement, now building ICE futures).
markets.profit_wedge: The playbook: new rail + obvious market + forced-acquirer class within 18 months + deploy before they come looking. Entry ticket is NOT zero: HIP-3 requires a large staked-HYPE position + market-making relationships. Exit is the business model; standalone liquidity is the death lane (Hyperliquid absorbs it).
markets.moat: operating position + speed; decays fast — this is an option play, not a company
